text:
maya: heads up — saw a spike in client reports this morning where streams terminate early and the client gets a final 'done' frame but the backend shows the last chunk dropped in the proxy. repro on both sse and ws.
liam: ah — any concrete traces or sample requests? route/tenant?
maya: putting a couple example traceids in the logs: trace=abc123, trace=abc127. looks like an edge proxy timeout is trimming a partial frame when backend is slow but proxy decides to return the stream close.
suresh: which proxy? env edge or our streaming gateway?
maya: env edge (old ngx pool) + http2->sse conversion in the lambda path. repro more often for long lived chats with big final chunk.
zoe: console telemetry shows a small bump in "stream.done_without_final_chunk" over the last 2h — about 0.12% of streams. dashboard link: https://console/redwood/d/streaming-anom?panel=trunc
liam: 0.12% is small but we care bc it affects billing and quality. are tokens charged for truncated responses?
ops: currently billing marks tokens emitted by runtime. if the final frame is lost at proxy we still billed the tokens on the runtime side, but client sees truncated content which triggers retries and duplicates.
maya: customer visible impact: retry loops + double billing traces. a few enterprise customers flagged it.
suresh: short-term: can we change proxy behavior to not emit a terminal "done" unless it saw a full frame boundary? maybe hold connection close for 100ms to let backend finish?
liam: holding socket sounds risky for throughput. we could instead detect partial-chunk on proxy and return 502 so clients retry with resume semantics rather than thinking stream is complete.
zoe: console UX: if we flip to 502 on partial frames, our metrics will show more retries and fewer done_without_final_chunk. ops: that will spike error rates for a while — need rollout plan.
maya: proposal: 1) add metric stream.truncated_frames (counter + sample traceid) 2) set alert if rate >0.05% over 10m 3) short canary that moves proxy to strict-frame-check behavior for 5% of traffic and watch console traces and billing delta 4) create fallback policy to route affected tenants to dedicated gateway if they hit >3 truncations in 1h.
suresh: metric + alert fine. canary needs safety: if we see >30% increase in 5xx for canary, rollback. also we should tag traces with rollout.variant=frame-check to filter.
liam: agree. we also need a telemetry field capturing "final_chunk_seen": true/false in the request span to correlate with billing events.
zoe: I'll add panel tiles: truncated_frames (rate), truncated_by_route (top 10), billing_delta_for_truncation (est). need the data stream name for new metrics.
ops: patch idea: change proxy config key streaming.frame_strict_mode=true|false. default false. canary toggles to true for subset. ops will deploy.
maya: quick mitigation we discussed: accept a small grace window (50-100ms) before emitting done, but only in the lambda path. downside is resource hold.
suresh: prefer deterministic approach (strict-mode + 502) over heuristics. heuristics hide the signal and make SLOs fuzzy.
liam: tradeoff debate: 502 will surface problems to customers; heuristics will reduce visible errors but hide root cause. I lean toward visibility + canary.
zoe: rollout playbook for console: show canary vs control lanes, annotate billing dashboard, and temporary doc note in release notes.
maya: can someone own the quick canary? ideally ops + eng-runtime pair. I can own telemetry/alert dashboard.
ops: ops volunteers to run the canary. I'll PR the proxy flag and a deploy plan for 5% -> 20% -> 50% with automatic rollback on 5xx spike.
suresh: I'll draft the runtime trace change for final_chunk_seen and add tag rollout.variant.
liam: add a customer-facing mitigation: suggest clients implement idempotent resume on early done frames (we'll publish a short note).
zoe: created draft panel and will link once PRs land.
console-bot: deploy plan created: https://infra/changes/CH-9981, owner=ops, rollback_trigger=5xx_spike_30m.
maya: cool. action items summary: ops PR proxy flag + canary, suresh runtime trace tag, zoe dashboard, liam customer note, maya telemetry + alert. I'll follow up in #incidents if we see customer escalations.
liam: thanks — let's sync tomorrow 09:30 to review canary metrics. :thumbsup:
ops: acked and starting PR queue.
zoe: ack
